text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliamentarian says Kuwaitis do not want Jordanians back in Kuwait, home for some 400,000 Palestinians and Jordanians prior to the 1990-91 Iraqi occupation. Many Kuwaitis say they cannot forgive Jordan and the Palestine Liberation Organisation for what they see as siding with Iraq during the crisis.
- Canadian commercial team arrives in Kuwait for talks on boosting bilateral trade.
- Health Ministry sets lower maximum nicotine and tar levels for imported cigarettes.
- Housing study puts population for 2015 at 3.8 million from a current two million people.
- Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah to undergo routine medical checks in London after December's annual Gulf Arab summit in Qatar.
- Kuwait closes 15 lottery shops. The conservative Gulf state bans lottery in compliance with the teachings of Islam.
- United Nations official in charge of disarming Iraq, Rolf Ekeus, meets Kuwait leaders.
